directAnswer: To update a web cookie, you can use JavaScript's `document.cookie` property to set a new value for the cookie with the same name.
summary: Updating a web cookie involves using JavaScript to modify the existing cookie value while ensuring the correct attributes are maintained.

sections.heading: Understanding Cookies
sections.body: Cookies are small pieces of data stored on the user's device by the web browser while browsing a website. They are used for various purposes, including session management and user preferences.

sections.heading: Cookie Attributes
sections.body: When updating a cookie, it's important to specify attributes such as expiration date, path, and domain to ensure the cookie behaves as intended.

steps.title: Access the Cookie
steps.detail: Use JavaScript to access the cookie you want to update by reading `document.cookie`.

steps.title: Modify the Cookie
steps.detail: Set the cookie with the same name and a new value using the syntax: `document.cookie = 'cookieName=newValue; expires=expirationDate; path=/';`.

steps.title: Verify the Update
steps.detail: Check the updated cookie by accessing `document.cookie` again to confirm the new value is set.

faqs.question: Can I set a cookie to expire immediately?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can set a cookie to expire immediately by setting the expiration date to a past date.

faqs.question: What happens if I don't specify a path when updating a cookie?
faqs.answer: If you don't specify a path, the cookie will only be accessible from the current page's path.

faqs.question: Are there limits on cookie size?
faqs.answer: Yes, most browsers limit cookies to about 4KB in size.

caveats: Cookies are domain-specific; ensure you are updating the cookie from the correct domain.
Some browsers may block third-party cookies, affecting updates.
